title: A Bowl of Citrus
description: Explore citrus names and the familiar parts that distinguish a peel, a segment, and a wedge.
cardDescription: Explore citrus names and the familiar parts that distinguish a peel, a segment, and a wedge.
focus: The clues describe fruit parts and tastes. Color is used as a familiar association rather than a rule for every variety.
solvingTip: Look for a whole fruit, an outer layer, or a cut portion.
words: Yellow citrus fruit commonly used for a sharp juice
Citrus fruit often green-skinned and used for a tart flavor
Citrus fruit whose name also identifies a color
Large citrus fruit often cut in half for serving
Small easy-peeling citrus related to the mandarin
To remove a citrus fruit's outer skin
Outer covering around a citrus fruit
Colored outermost citrus skin used for flavor
Pale layer beneath the colored citrus skin
One natural section inside a citrus fruit
Liquid released when citrus fruit is squeezed
Plant structure sometimes found inside a citrus segment
Thick pointed piece cut from a citrus fruit

answerNotes.PITH: Pith is the pale layer beneath the colored skin. Zest refers to the colored outermost part instead.
answerNotes.SEGMENT: A segment is a natural section. A wedge is a cut shape that may contain more than one segment.
answerNotes.ZEST: Zest names a flavorful outer skin layer here. The word can also describe lively enthusiasm.
answerNotes.ORANGE: Orange names both a fruit and a color. The food setting determines the noun meaning in this clue.

title: A Basket of Berries
description: Browse familiar berry names, their small parts, and the words describing gathering and preserving them.
cardDescription: Browse familiar berry names, their small parts, and the words describing gathering and preserving them.
focus: The clues identify ordinary food names. The kitchen meaning of berry is used rather than a technical botanical classification.
solvingTip: Use short fruit-part and action words to cross the longer berry names.
words: Red fruit commonly pictured with tiny seedlike structures outside
Small round fruit often blue when ripe
Soft fruit made of clustered juicy units around a hollow center
Dark clustered fruit retaining a solid central core
Tart red fruit commonly made into a holiday sauce
Common kitchen word for a small juicy fruit
Small plant support remaining on a picked fruit
Tiny plant structure associated with many fruits
Flat green plant part sometimes found in a picked basket
Liquid released from a soft fruit
Sharp rather than sugary in flavor
Woven container used to gather small fruits
Mature and ready for eating, as fruit
To remove fruit from a plant for gathering

answerNotes.RASPBERRY: A picked raspberry usually has a hollow center. A blackberry retains its central core.
answerNotes.STRAWBERRY: The small structures outside a strawberry are fruits called achenes, each containing a seed. The clue uses their familiar appearance.
answerNotes.JAM: Jam commonly retains fruit pulp. It differs from a clear jelly made from strained juice.
answerNotes.PICK: Pick is a gathering action here. It does not name a small tool used to pluck a string.

title: On the Spice Shelf
description: Open familiar spice jars through names, plant sources, and the words for powders and aromas.
cardDescription: Open familiar spice jars through names, plant sources, and the words for powders and aromas.
focus: The clues identify flavorings by their source or familiar use. Containers and forms provide shorter everyday answers.
solvingTip: Look for a spice, the way it is prepared, or the container holding it.
words: Warm aromatic spice made from tree bark
Strong spice consisting of a dried flower bud
Seed spice commonly grated into sweet or savory food
Aromatic rhizome used fresh or dried as a spice
Spice commonly ground from dried peppercorns
Red powder made from dried peppers
Aromatic seed spice used in many savory dishes
Seed spice associated with a licorice-like flavor
Flavoring traditionally obtained from cured orchid pods
Aromatic plant material used to flavor food
Rigid container holding a small quantity of spice
Removable top closing a spice jar
Fine dry form of a ground spice
Noticeable smell from an opened spice jar

answerNotes.CLOVE: A spice clove is a flower bud. It is not one division of a garlic bulb.
answerNotes.NUTMEG: Nutmeg is a seed used as a spice. Mace is a different spice from its surrounding covering.
answerNotes.ANISE: Anise is associated with a licorice-like taste. It is a different plant from true licorice.
answerNotes.POWDER: Powder describes the fine physical form. It does not name one particular spice.

title: Herbs at the Kitchen Window
description: Explore familiar herbs and the small plant parts gathered around a kitchen windowsill.
cardDescription: Explore familiar herbs and the small plant parts gathered around a kitchen windowsill.
focus: The clues name plants, their parts, and small quantities used in cooking vocabulary. They do not prescribe a recipe.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a whole herb, one plant part, or a quantity word.
words: Aromatic herb commonly paired with tomatoes
Small-leaved herb whose name sounds like time
Gray-green aromatic herb often used in savory stuffing
Fragrant herb associated with a refreshing flavor
Feathery-leaved herb associated with some pickles
Leafy herb commonly used as a garnish
Slender onion-family herb with hollow leaves
Woody aromatic herb with narrow needlelike leaves
Container holding a kitchen herb plant
Flat plant part picked from many herbs
Smell released by an aromatic herb
Small quantity held between the fingertips

answerNotes.THYME: Thyme and time sound alike. The herb meaning determines the spelling.
answerNotes.SPRIG: A sprig is a small leafy stem. It names a plant piece rather than a measured weight.
answerNotes.PINCH: A pinch is an informal small quantity. It does not specify a fixed exact measure.
answerNotes.SAGE: Sage names an herb here. The same word can mean a wise person in another setting.

title: Preserves in the Pantry
description: Read familiar preserve labels through jars, condiments, and the words describing their contents.
cardDescription: Read familiar preserve labels through jars, condiments, and the words describing their contents.
focus: The clues identify food forms and storage objects. They do not give processing instructions or storage-time advice.
solvingTip: Look for a food, a liquid ingredient, or part of the container.
words: Preserve commonly made from strained fruit juice
Food preserved in a brine or acidic mixture
Seasoned condiment made from fruit or vegetables
Top used to close a preserve jar
Written marker naming a jar’s contents
Plant produce used in many sweet preserves
Sweet crystals used in many fruit preserves
Acidic liquid used in many pickled foods
Horizontal storage surface in a pantry

answerNotes.JELLY: A clear fruit jelly commonly uses strained juice. Jam usually contains more fruit pulp.
answerNotes.BRINE: Brine is a salt-water solution. The clue names the liquid, not a complete preservation method.
answerNotes.CHUTNEY: Chutney is a seasoned condiment. Its ingredients and texture vary among traditions and recipes.
answerNotes.RELISH: Relish is a chopped condiment here. The same word can mean enthusiastic enjoyment.
